en: Abu Bakr ibn Khallad al-Bahili and Ahmad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Hakam narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abd Rabbihi ibn Sa'id, from Abu Salamah, who said: "I used to see a dream that would make me sick." He said: "Then I met Abu Qatadah, and he said: 'I too used to see a dream that would make me sick, until I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "The righteous dream is from Allah; so when one of you sees what he likes, let him not tell it to anyone except one whom he loves. And if he sees what he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times and seek refuge with Allah from the evil of Satan and its evil, and let him not tell it to anyone, for then it will never harm him."'

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abd Rabbihi ibn Sa'id, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Qatadah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "A righteous dream is from Allah, and a bad dream is from Satan. So whoever sees a dream and dislikes something of it, let him spit lightly to his left and seek refuge with Allah from Satan; it will not harm him, and let him not inform anyone of it. But if he sees a good dream, let him rejoice, and let him not inform anyone except one whom he loves."

Qutaybah and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated it to us, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (Second chain) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab—meaning al-Thaqafi—narrated to us; (Third chain) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; all of them from Yahya ibn Sa'id, with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of al-Thaqafi, Abu Salamah said: "Indeed, I used to see a dream..." but the words of Abu Salamah to the end of the hadith are not in the narration of al-Layth or Ibn Numayr. And Ibn Rumh added in his narration of this hadith: "and let him turn over from the side on which he was lying."

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us: Sulayman—meaning Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman saying: I heard Abu Qatadah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "A good dream is from Allah, and a bad dream is from Satan. So when one of you sees something he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times and seek refuge with Allah from its evil, for it will not harm him." He said: "I used to see a dream that was heavier on me than a mountain, but as soon as I heard this hadith, I did not care about it."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me; (Second chain) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—they said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us; both from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission. And in their hadith there is no mention of "I would shiver with fever from it." And in the hadith of Yunus it was added: "let him spit to his left three times when he awakes from his sleep."

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, the freed slave of the family of Talhah, and Abd Rabbihi and Yahya, the two sons of Sa'id, and Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqamah, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Qatadah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, and he did not mention in their hadith the statement of Abu Salamah: "I used to see a dream that made me shiver with fever, except that I was not wrapped in a cloak."

Amr al-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Uyaynah—and the wording is that of Ibn Abi Umar: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, who said: "I used to see a dream that would make me shiver with fever, except that I was not wrapped in a cloak, until I met Abu Qatadah and mentioned that to him. He said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "A good dream is from Allah, and a bad dream is from Satan. So if one of you has a nightmare that he dislikes, let him spit lightly to his left three times and seek refuge with Allah from its evil, for it will not harm him."'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever plays with nardashir (dice) is as though he dipped his hand into the flesh of swine and its blood."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id al-Thaqafi narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, from Yuhannis, the freed slave of Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: While we were traveling with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) at al-Arj, a poet appeared reciting poetry. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Seize the devil!" or "Restrain the devil! For a man's belly to be filled with pus is better for him than to be filled with poetry."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "For the belly of one of you to be filled with pus that eats it up from inside is better than for it to be filled with poetry."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hafs and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; both of them from al-A'mash; (Third chain) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "For a man's belly to be filled with pus that eats it up from inside is better than for it to be filled with poetry." Abu Bakr said: Except that Hafs did not say "that eats it up from inside."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Yahya ibn Zakariyya informed us, from Isra'il, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "Indeed, the truest word a poet ever uttered is the word of Labid: 'Verily, everything besides Allah is vain.'" And he added nothing to that.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The truest line of poetry that poets ever said is: 'Verily, everything besides Allah is vain.'"

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to me: Sufyan narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The truest line of poetry that a poet ever said is: 'Verily, everything besides Allah is vain.' And Ibn Abi al-Salt was near to accepting Islam."

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr: Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The truest word a poet ever uttered is the word of Labid: 'Verily, everything besides Allah is vain.' And Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt was near to accepting Islam."

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah and Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di narrated to me, both from Sharik; Ibn Hujr said: Sharik informed us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The most poetic word that the Arabs ever spoke is the word of Labid: 'Verily, everything besides Allah is vain.'"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman informed us; (Second chain) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; both of them from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ta'ifi, from Amr ibn al-Sharid, from his father, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asked me to recite poetry..." similar to the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, and he added: He said: "He was very close to accepting Islam." And in the hadith of Ibn Mahdi he said: "Indeed, he was close to accepting Islam in his poetry."

Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, both from Ibn Uyaynah; Ibn Abi Umar said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Amr ibn al-Sharid, from his father, who said: One day I rode behind the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he said: "Do you have any of the poetry of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt with you?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Go on." So I recited a verse to him, and he said: "Go on." Then I recited another verse to him, and he said: "Go on," until I had recited one hundred verses to him. And Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ahmad ibn Abdah narrated it to me, both from Ibn Uyaynah, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Amr ibn al-Sharid or Ya'qub ibn Asim, from al-Sharid, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had me ride behind him..." and he mentioned something similar.

Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli, Abu al-Tahir, and Ahmad ibn Isa narrated to me—Ahmad said: narrated to us, and the other two said: informed us: Ibn Wahb: Makhramah informed me, from his father, from Nafi', who said: When Ibn Umar fumigated himself with incense, he would fumigate with pure aloeswood that was not scented with anything else, and with camphor that he mixed with the aloeswood, and then he said: "In this manner the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to fumigate."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, both from al-Muqri'; Abu Bakr said: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub: Ubaydullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever is offered sweet basil, let him not refuse it, for it is light to carry and pleasant in fragrance."

Amr al-Naqid narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Khulayd ibn Ja'far and al-Mustamir—they said: We heard Abu Nadrah narrating from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) mentioned a woman from the Children of Israel who stuffed her ring with musk, and musk is the best of scents.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Shu'bah: Khulayd ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "There was a short woman from the Children of Israel who used to walk with two tall women. So she made two legs of wood and a gold ring that had a closed compartment, which she stuffed with musk—and it is the best of scents. Then she walked between the two women and they did not recognize her, and she motioned with her hand like this." And Shu'bah shook his hand.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should say, 'My soul has become wicked,' but let him say, 'My soul has become uneasy.'"
Abu Kurayb narrated it to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala' narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us; both of them from Hisham, from his father, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should ever say, 'My soul has become wicked,' but let him say, 'My soul has become uneasy.'" This is the hadith of Abu Kurayb; while Abu Bakr said: from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he did not mention "but."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which was: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should say: 'Serve water to your lord,' 'Feed your lord,' or 'Help your lord perform ablution.' And none of you should say: 'My lord.' Rather, let him say: 'My master,' or 'My patron.' And none of you should say: 'My slave boy,' or 'My slave girl.' Rather, let him say: 'My lad,' 'My lass,' or 'My young boy.'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (Second chain) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us; both from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission. And in their hadith: "And the servant should not say to his master: 'My patron.'" And it was added in the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah: "For indeed, your Patron is Allah, the Mighty and Sublime."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should say: 'My slave,' for all of you are the slaves of Allah; but let him say: 'My lad.' And the servant should not say: 'My lord,' but let him say: 'My master.'"

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—they said: Isma'il—and he is Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "None of you should ever say: 'My male slave' or 'My female slave.' All of you are the slaves of Allah, and all of your women are the maidservants of Allah; but let him say: 'My young boy,' 'My young girl,' 'My lad,' or 'My lass.'"

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, who said: I heard Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from his father, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not say 'al-karm' (for grapevines), but say 'al-inab' (grapes) and 'al-habalah' (the vine)."
